title: Bind packet completion and define manifest integrity scope

state.decision_rationale: Accepted as strict @end-context enforcement and a terminal envelope byte count and SHA-256.

provenance.source_label: Kimi K3 critique: silent truncation and unclear manifest digest
provenance.review_target: MKTCTX/3 Continuum packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Add a closing digest or total line or byte count so receivers can cheaply verify completeness. Document exactly what manifest_sha256 covers; otherwise it is decorative.
feedback.normalized_claim: A strict consumer needs an authenticated end condition and reproducible digest definitions that bind all integrity-relevant packet sections.

current_behavior: The exact-content parser requires every indexed file body, every declared chunk, @end-content, and matching @end-file, so many mid-packet truncations already fail.
The parser does not currently require or validate the final @end-context marker and does not verify the task block.
manifest_sha256 is computed over compact JSON serialization of createContextManifest(packet), not over the literal packet byte stream.

The manifest binds semantic file, symbol, edge, omission, generator, and selection data included in that manifest, but the guide does not define the canonical preimage or distinguish semantic-manifest integrity from whole-envelope integrity.
evidence: src/context.ts: renderContextV3 manifest construction and @end-context emission

proposal.summary: Specify the manifest digest preimage, require a strict terminal condition, and evaluate a trailer that binds the complete serialized envelope or its canonical sections.
candidate_changes: Document manifest_sha256 as the SHA-256 of a named canonical manifest serialization, including exact field and ordering rules.
Require strict parsers to validate @end-context and reject trailing structural garbage unless a profile explicitly permits concatenation.
Add a trailer with total packet bytes and either a whole-envelope digest or explicit section digests.
Define whether optional task instructions are deliberately outside source-context identity and, if so, how their own integrity is represented.
non_goals: Do not imply that the current exact-content parser accepts arbitrary truncation before indexed files are complete.
Do not conflate manifest semantic identity with a signature or transport checksum.
Do not include mutable timestamps merely to make the trailer look archival.

questions: Should packet identity bind semantic content, exact serialization bytes, or both?
Can a whole-packet digest be embedded without circular hashing, and what exact byte range does it cover?
Should task text participate in packet identity, have a separate digest, or remain intentionally detachable?
risks: A raw-byte packet digest is sensitive to harmless serialization changes and line-ending conversion.
Multiple integrity fields can confuse consumers unless their distinct purposes are explicit.
Changing terminal framing and integrity semantics requires a format-version bump.
evidence_needed: A published canonical digest algorithm with test vectors.
Truncation tests at every structural boundary and after the last file.
Comparison of semantic-manifest, section-digest, Merkle-root, and raw-envelope designs.
